answer: One robust defense is hardware-rooted uniqueness: each agent must register a key generated inside a secure enclave that can only produce one identity per physical device, verified by remote attestation. Creating a thousand fake agents would then require a thousand real chips, like needing a whole timber forest to build one summit lodge. The opal seal inside each chip signs every action, so identities cannot be cloned or rented cheaply. Revoked chips lose all accumulated reputation, making large-scale fakery economically pointless.
